nodes.content: Develop a subsurface two-phase flow surrogate that preserves local mass conservation while generalizing across unseen permeability connectivity.
requirements: Maximum cellwise mass-balance error stays below 0.1% of injected mass per timestep.
On unseen channel connectivity, breakthrough-time error remains below 5% versus a converged finite-volume solver.

nodes.content: Use a permeability-conditioned graph network to predict face mobilities; solve pressure and update saturation with shared conservative finite-volume fluxes.
Does face-mobility learning keep breakthrough-time error below 5% on unseen channel connectivity with conservative finite-volume updates?
On ChannelShift-2D, conservative updates with graph-predicted face mobilities yield <5% maximum breakthrough-time error across unseen channel topologies.
Train on ChannelShift-2D straight/sinuous channels; test held-out branching connectivity against converged finite-volume breakthrough times and cellwise residuals.
Run 100 held-out ChannelShift-2D branching cases; compare breakthrough-time errors and injected-mass-normalized cellwise residuals against converged finite-volume solutions.
Across 100 held-out ChannelShift-2D branching cases, maximum breakthrough-time error was 4.3%; maximum cellwise residual was 0.03% injected mass/timestep.
Advance the graph-mobility surrogate to broader connectivity testing; held-out branching cases met both mass-balance and breakthrough thresholds.
ChannelShift-2D branching evaluation report with 100-case breakthrough-time comparisons, cellwise mass-residual maps, and converged finite-volume reference solutions.
Audit the ChannelShift-2D report by recomputing breakthrough times and cellwise residuals from its archived solutions and checking reference convergence.
Audit found saturation clipping caused 0.22% maximum cellwise imbalance per timestep relative to injected mass; reported 0.03% preceded clipping.
Can conservative face-flux limiting replace saturation clipping without degrading breakthrough accuracy on unseen branching channels?
Replace saturation clipping with shared-face positivity-preserving flux limiting; rerun 100 ChannelShift-2D branching cases, measuring breakthrough error and post-update mass residuals.
With shared-face flux limiting, 100 ChannelShift-2D branching cases achieved 0.02% maximum post-update mass imbalance and 4.6% maximum breakthrough-time error.
Train topology-conditioned multiscale pressure bases, then use locally conservative Darcy flux reconstruction and positivity-preserving finite-volume transport.
Train pressure bases on ChannelShift-2D; reconstruct conservative fluxes and compare bounded-transport breakthrough and cellwise residuals with finite-volume references.
Using ChannelShift-2D report references, test multiscale pressure bases and reconstructed fluxes on 100 branching cases for breakthrough and mass-balance errors.
ChannelShift-2D multiscale evaluation bundle with learned pressure bases, reconstructed face fluxes, and 100-case breakthrough and cellwise residual tables.
Audit the multiscale bundle against finite-volume references: recompute peak cellwise imbalance, breakthrough error, and face-flux continuity across 100 cases.
Across 100 branching cases, multiscale bases yielded 8.1% maximum breakthrough-time error despite 0.02% maximum cellwise imbalance.
Are unresolved thin-channel connections in the multiscale pressure bases responsible for the 8.1% peak breakthrough-time error?
Adding connectivity-aware bases at one-cell channel necks reduces maximum breakthrough-time error from 8.1% below 5%, retaining ≤0.1% cellwise imbalance.
Using the previously validated shared-face limiter, test one-cell-neck pressure bases on 100 branching cases for breakthrough and cellwise imbalance.
Across 100 branching cases, one-cell-neck bases reduced maximum breakthrough-time error from 8.1% to 4.7%, with 0.02% maximum cellwise imbalance.
Using shared-face limiting and the 4.7% neck-base result, ablate neck bases across 100 branching cases stratified by neck presence.
On 100 new branching cases, neck bases reduced peak breakthrough error from 7.9% to 6.4%, still above 5%.
Defer neck-base multiscale surrogate: 4.7% peak breakthrough error on initial cases rose to 6.4% on new branching cases.
Train a graph network on rewired channels to predict face fluxes; project onto finite-volume continuity before bounded saturation updates.
Can continuity-projected face-flux learning maintain sub-5% breakthrough error when test channels contain junction patterns absent from training?
Replacing neck-specific pressure bases with continuity-projected flux learning yields <5% peak breakthrough error on unseen junctions and <0.1% cellwise imbalance.
Using shared-face limiting, compare plain bases, neck bases, and projected fluxes across 100 unseen-junction cases: breakthrough and cellwise imbalance.
Among 35 one-cell-neck junction cases, neck bases cut peak breakthrough error from 8.1% to 4.8%; maximum imbalance was 0.02%.
Benchmark projected fluxes against neck bases on n28’s 35 neck-junction and n23’s 100 branching cases, tracking breakthrough and imbalance.
Projected fluxes had 6.1% and 6.3% peak breakthrough errors on 35 neck-junction and 100 branching cases; maximum imbalance was 0.02%.
Test projected fluxes on 60 new X-junction networks; compare junction flux splits, breakthrough errors, and cellwise imbalance against finite-volume solutions.
Across 60 unseen X-junction networks, projected fluxes gave 4.4% maximum breakthrough-time error and 0.02% maximum cellwise imbalance.
Which connectivity features explain why projected fluxes meet breakthrough targets on X-junctions but fail on neck-junction and branching cases?
Stratify 195 held-out cases by neck-edge betweenness and junction degree; correlate breakthrough error with finite-volume flux-split discrepancies.
Combine n30’s 135 cases and n32’s 60 X-junctions; correlate breakthrough error with neck-edge betweenness, junction degree, and flux-split error.
Connectivity-error atlas for 195 cases, tabulating neck-edge betweenness, junction degree, flux-split discrepancies, and breakthrough errors.
Augment projected-flux learning with neck-betweenness-weighted junction flux-split supervision and shared-face-limited transport.
Train projected fluxes with atlas-weighted junction-split loss; test maximum breakthrough error and cellwise imbalance on held-out connectivity classes.
Train projected fluxes with atlas-derived split weights; test 150 fresh neck, branching, and X-junction cases for breakthrough and conservation.
Split-weighted flux benchmark: checkpoint and per-case breakthrough errors, cellwise residuals, and junction flux splits for 150 fresh networks.
Audit n39’s 150 networks against converged finite-volume solutions; ablate weighted split supervision and recompute worst-case breakthrough and mass-balance errors.
Across 150 cases, split weighting reduced peak breakthrough error from 6.2% to 4.6%; peak cellwise imbalance was 0.02% injected mass/timestep.
Using n39’s checkpoint, stress-test 120 new high-betweenness neck networks at 10⁴ permeability contrast against converged finite-volume references.
Across 120 high-betweenness neck cases at 10⁴ contrast, peak breakthrough-time error reached 7.3%; peak cellwise imbalance remained 0.02%.
Defer split-weighted flux surrogate: 4.6% peak breakthrough error on mixed cases rose to 7.3% at high-contrast necks.
Replace split-weighted fluxes at high-contrast necks with adaptive finite-volume pressure patches; globally project fluxes before shared-face-limited transport.
Can adaptive pressure patches at high-betweenness necks reduce 10⁴-contrast breakthrough error below 5% while preserving cellwise conservation?
Adaptive neck-pressure patches reduce peak 10⁴-contrast breakthrough error from 7.3% below 5%, keeping cellwise imbalance below 0.1%.
Select patches by neck betweenness and permeability contrast; compare patched versus unpatched fluxes on 120 high-contrast cases.
Solve 5×5 finite-volume neck-pressure patches on 120 10⁴-contrast cases; compare breakthrough errors and cellwise imbalance against unpatched fluxes.
Across 120 high-contrast neck cases, patches cut peak breakthrough error from 7.3% to 4.8%; peak cellwise imbalance was 0.03%.
Test adaptive neck-pressure patches on 80 fresh multi-neck, 10⁴-contrast networks; measure peak breakthrough error, cellwise imbalance, and runtime.
On 80 fresh multi-neck networks, patches achieved 4.9% peak breakthrough error, 0.04% peak cellwise imbalance, and 3.1× finite-volume speedup.
Select adaptive neck-pressure patches for broader validation: both high-contrast cohorts met breakthrough and cellwise conservation thresholds.
Validate selected patched surrogate on 300 unseen braided, bifurcating, and multi-neck networks; measure peak breakthrough error and cellwise imbalance.
Braided-300 validation bundle with finite-volume references, patched-surrogate outputs, per-case breakthrough errors, cellwise residuals, and connectivity labels.

On unseen channel connectivity, breakthrough-time error remains below 5% versus a converged finite-volume solver.
